_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_onboard_perinstance_baseurl_and_bareword_claims.md (PR #41, 2026-06-06).

handfixes.summary: HUDU_BASE_URL (per-tenant API base) is in manifest.json user_config + mcp_config.env + mcp-install.md + README; the press shipped only the HUDU_API_KEY secret
handfixes.why: Hudu's API base is per-tenant (https://<sub>.huducloud.com/api/v1). The press derives auth_env_vars from the SECRET only (HUDU_API_KEY), treating the base URL as a verify-time override, so manifest user_config + mcp_config.env, mcp-install.md, and the README auth example all shipped with only the key while config.go's default base URL is a NON-FUNCTIONAL placeholder (your-domain.huducloud.com) - the .mcpb extension and every env example point at a dead domain and fail silently. verify_all stays green (no gate checks env-var COMPLETENESS vs config.go). Hand-added HUDU_BASE_URL to manifest + mcp-install + README (server.json stays credential-only to match the n-central precedent). A reprint drops the base URL again.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press: per-instance connectors should carry every required non-secret config var (base_url/region/tenant) into manifest user_config + mcp env + docs, not just the secret. Sibling of project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar (NAME mismatch) - this is env-var OMISSION.

handfixes.summary: Docs reference `assets list-by-company <company_id>` with the real positional, not the press's bogus `--company-id` flag form
handfixes.why: check_cli_claims only validates full <binary> ... invocations, so it missed (a) a bare-command backtick ref `assets list-by-company --company-id <id>` (the real command takes a positional <company_id>; --company-id is 'unknown flag') and (b) a trailing positional after a zero-positional command (`api-info get`). Both were generator-emitted prose in the vendored SKILL.md + guide.md; only the fresh-context adversarial reviewer catches them. Corrected to the real positional form. A reprint re-emits the bogus flag form.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Not fully press-encodable - the adversarial reviewer must check bare-command refs AND trailing positionals semantically, built from agent-context. Sibling of project_onboard_missing_required_positional_defect.

handfixes.summary: Non-affiliation banner does not double-period a trademark owner ending in 'Inc.'
handfixes.why: A --trademark-owner ending in 'Inc.' + the template's trailing '.' produced 'Inc..' in the README non-affiliation banner. Stripped to a single period. A reprint with the same owner string reintroduces the double period.

handfixes.summary: Five Hudu IPAM-family list endpoints (ip-addresses, networks, vlans, vlan-zones, rack-storage-items) are NON-paginated: sync/list send them neither page_size NOR page (both 400), the --page-size + --page flags and the page-size + page MCP args are removed for them, and sync fetches the full collection in one request
handfixes.why: issues #153 + #158: the press emits a single global pagination profile and registers every list endpoint as paginated. Hudu rejects page_size on these five with HTTP 400 ('page_size is not a valid filter parameter.'; rack-storage-items: '...not a valid parameter.'). #153 carved out page_size but ASSUMED they page by `page` and walked page=1,2,...; #158 proved that assumption wrong - they reject `page` with the same 400 (they are non-paginated and return the whole collection in one response, confirmed on a live huducloud tenant + the n8n-nodes-hudu project, which likewise removed pagination here). Fix: resourceRejectsPageSize() now means 'non-paginated' - sync sends no pagination params and stops after the single response (the page-int fallback and more-pages walk both opt these out), the 5 list cmds drop both --page-size and --page, and code_orch.go drops both the page-size and page MCP args. A reprint re-adds page_size+page everywhere and re-breaks all five.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: the profiler must support PER-ENDPOINT pagination shape, not one global profile for the whole API. Some endpoints accept page+page_size, some are non-paginated. Filed as a printing-press-retro. Sibling of project_ninjaone_after_id_pagination_defect.

handfixes.summary: determinePaginationDefaults() sets cursorType "page" so the ?page=N page-int fallback is live; cursorType "" disabled it and silently truncated every multi-page resource at the first 100 rows
handfixes.why: issue #158 (Bug 2): the press emitted cursorType "" while cursorParam was "page". The page-int fallback in sync.go guards on cursorType=="page", so with "" it was dead code - and Hudu returns no body cursor, so sync could not advance past page 1 for ANY resource. v0.1.0 truncated silently; the 4.24 engine's new 'data may be truncated' warning surfaced it on the high-cardinality resources (expirations/folders/public-photos/relations/procedure-tasks). Fix: cursorType "page". Sibling connectors generated correctly (connectwise-manage has cursorType "page"); this was a Hudu-specific profiler miss. A reprint re-emits cursorType "".
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: when cursorParam resolves to a page-integer spelling (page/page_number/...), cursorType must be set to 'page', not left ''. Filed in the same printing-press-retro as the per-endpoint pagination shape.

handfixes.summary: procedure-tasks sync detects a repeated primary-key set before upsert and reconciles sync_complete.total to distinct stored rows
handfixes.why: Issue #183 confirmed on a live Hudu tenant that /procedure_tasks ignores page and page_size. The generated page-int walk fetched the complete collection, requested page 2, received the collection again, and upserted every row before the duplicate fingerprint stopped the loop. sync_complete.total therefore counted successful conflict updates while the unique-ID cache correctly contained one set of rows. The duplicate guard now compares the complete sorted primary-key set before upsert, preserving the validation request for deployments that honor pagination and handling response reordering or field updates. The completion metric is reconciled to SQLite so overlapping pages and pre-existing rows cannot inflate or understate the stored-row count. A reprint restores the duplicate upsert and misleading metric.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: the profiler must support per-endpoint pagination shape, including endpoints that accept but ignore pagination parameters and return the complete collection. Filed as mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3481 closed 2026-08-15 as not planned (one-vendor retro grab-bag; upstream said reopen if still biting on current main), no fix landed; this hand-fix is permanent unless re-filed; do NOT cite #3481 as open.

handfixes.summary: Flat `sync` skips the matchers resource (with a warning) unless integration_id is supplied, because Hudu's /matchers returns HTTP 500 without one and there is no integrations-list endpoint to enumerate IDs
handfixes.why: issue #159: /matchers requires an integration_id query param (Hudu 500s without it). The press registers matchers as a flat-syncable list, so every `sync` 500'd on it and exhausted retries. Fix: syncResource skips matchers when the user did not pass integration_id (via --resource-param matchers:integration_id=<id> / --global-param), via the new syncUserParams.hasParam() accessor; users fetch per-integration with `matchers list --integration-id <id>`. A reprint re-adds matchers to the flat sync set and re-breaks it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: an endpoint with a REQUIRED query param that flat-list sync cannot supply (and no enumerable parent) should be excluded from the default sync set, not registered as flat-syncable. Sibling of the unresolved-path-key skip already in sync.go.

handfixes.summary: sync pages the relations resource at page_size=25 (per-resource resourcePageSize override), not the global 100; relations list also defaults --page-size to 25
handfixes.why: issue #167: Hudu's /relations endpoint returns HTTP 500 when sync walks it at the global page_size=100 (page-2 request onward), so every sync failed on relations and exhausted retries. A live relations list at page_size 100/25/1 all succeed, so relations is NOT non-paginated like the IPAM family (resourceRejectsPageSize) - it accepts page_size and pages by ?page=N, it just 500s at size 100. Fix: resourcePageSize() returns 25 for relations (Hudu's documented default, and the size n8n-nodes-hudu uses to retrieve all relations), applied to pageSize.limit in syncResource; relations_list.go defaults --page-size to 25 so manual paging does not hit the same 500. A reprint re-emits the global 100 for relations and re-breaks sync.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: PER-ENDPOINT page_size (some endpoints 500 at the API max page size and need a smaller one). Filed in the same printing-press-retro as the per-endpoint pagination shape. Sibling of ipam-endpoints-reject-page-size.

handfixes.summary: sync has an --exclude flag that drops named resources from the effective set (after --resources or the default), with loud validation of unknown names
handfixes.why: issue #169: sync ran every resource on every run with no way to skip the slow ones (public-photos/procedures/procedure-tasks), making a scheduled daily sync impractical; the only workaround was to enumerate all 20+ resources to keep via --resources. Added --exclude (StringSliceVar) plus validateExcludeNames (rejects unknown names, same contract as --resource-param) and filterExcludedResources (order-preserving set difference). A reprint drops the flag and both helpers.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press gap: sync should offer a native --exclude complement to --resources. Filed in the printing-press-retro.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. server.json gained: HUDU_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `sync --phase-trace` emits a per-resource sync_phases event splitting wall time into queue wait, API fetch, rate-limit wait, retry wait, ID extraction and SQLite upsert (issue #195)
handfixes.why: issue #195: a production tenant reported lightweight Hudu resources taking disproportionately long in a multi-resource sync, and the only number the sync emitted was one per-resource duration_ms that folds six different things together. It also starts AFTER a worker dequeues the resource, so the interval the reporter's own hypothesis points at was not merely unattributed, it was outside the measurement entirely. queue_wait_ms is the fifth phase the issue's acceptance criteria omit and the reason the work channel now carries a syncWorkItem with an enqueue timestamp instead of a bare string. The client-side split (rate_limit_wait_ms and retry_wait_ms subtracted out of api_fetch_ms) needs a hook inside internal/client, which is why RequestTrace lives there and is plumbed through the context: without it a 429 storm reads as slow server time. Entirely opt-in - with the flag unset no trace is installed, every helper is a nil-receiver no-op, and the emitted event stream is byte-identical to before, verified by diffing two real CLI runs. The event carries durations and counts only: no credential, no URL, no response body. Offline fixtures (local HTTP plus real SQLite contention) show queue_wait dominant for 4 of 6 resources at concurrency 2, and store_upsert dominant for all 8 at concurrency 8 against an instant server, which proves the mechanism is REACHABLE - not that it is the dominant phase in the reporter's tenant, which needs their tenant to settle. Follow-up inside this same PR: dominant() seeded its accumulator at -1 and evaluated queue_wait first, so an all-zero trace (a resource that failed before it reached the API) reported dominant_phase=queue_wait and the "none" branch was unreachable; queue_wait also won every tie. It now requires strict dominance and returns "none" for an all-zero trace and for a tie, proven at the real binary: `sync --resources a --phase-trace` against an unreachable base URL emits dominant_phase="none" where it emitted "queue_wait" before. The event is also marshalled instead of hand-formatted, because --resources takes the resource name from the operator and a name containing a quote emitted a line no JSON parser could read.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit phase-level sync diagnostics for every connector, because the shape is generic: the work channel, the fixed worker pool, the per-resource duration that starts at dequeue, and the store's single write mutex held through tx.Commit() are all template code. 61 of 65 connectors take writeMu directly in UpsertBatch and the remaining 4 take it through lockForWrite(), so every connector in the fleet serializes its workers on one lock with no way to see it. queue_wait_ms in particular cannot be back-derived by any consumer of today's events.

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown). Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: onboard is refused over MCP: --template (reads a local JSON file) and --init (writes one) are declared host-file flags, and a process the MCP server spawned refuses onboard entirely; --init honours --dry-run; --init replaces an existing template only with --yes
handfixes.why: onboard --template names a local file it reads and --init writes one. Press 4.34.0 drops a flag from the MCP tool schema and refuses it only when the command declares it, so an MCP tool argument could make the server read or write a host file. Two layers, either one alone refuses: the mcp:read-flags / mcp:write-flags annotations, and a RunE guard on HUDU_MCP_CHILD. Found by check_mcp_file_flags.py and Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 reprint.

handfixes.why: The preview named --company while the folder POST used the template's own company_id when present, so the write could land in another customer's Hudu company. Codex round 1 on the 4.34.0 reprint.

handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 dogfood scans novel doctor files and fails on any host literal that does not resolve; the shipped-placeholder check now takes the value from config.ShippedBaseURL() so it stays exactly the placeholder a fresh install uses.

handfixes.summary: audit and audit expirations are registered with literal AddCommand calls so the command walker sees them
handfixes.why: Dogfood walks only literal AddCommand calls; without them `audit expirations` false-matched the root `expirations` command. A reprint restores the generated line and dogfood fails visibly.

handfixes.summary: the unused press query-retention helpers are removed while no hudu command calls them
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 emits retainCLIQueryParams / retainExplicitQueryParams, which no hudu command calls, and dogfood fails on dead helper functions. Restore them only if a command starts calling them.

handfixes.why: The 4.24 two-argument classifyAPIError no longer exists in 4.34.0 (the build breaks), and dogfood's novel-host gate rejects a help example on a non-reserved host.

handfixes.summary: Hudu tenant secrets (vault password/otp_secret and the values of password-type asset layout fields) are withheld by RESOURCE, not by body shape, via the shared rule in internal/huduprotect. do/doRead/doMutation put an answeredURLs holder in the ctx; doInternal records resp.Request.URL after every successful httpClient.Do, and a response is protected when the requested path OR any answered URL names the vault (path contains asset_password, lowercased and percent-decoded until stable, query ignored) or assets (a path segment equal to assets). Any non-success body from a protected URL becomes a fixed withheld message inside doInternal (2xx HTML too; no AnnotateTransportBlock); the APIError keeps method, masked path and status. Successful vault bodies keep an exact key allowlist (no _at suffix rule); successful asset bodies get every field entry decided by its own field_type AND the layout's type (GET /asset_layouts/{id}, memoized per client, never through the asset rule; a failed lookup is secret), the decided type written as field_type and a non-empty secret value replaced by [withheld: password field]; unclassifiable bodies are errors. GetWithHeaders applies the same rule to cached bodies. A request body carrying the placeholder is refused before the wire. The store funnel mergeIncomingResourceData scrubs the MERGED row for every write; StoreSchemaVersion 14 rewrites existing vault and asset rows (resources, asset_passwords, assets, resources_fts) once with secure_delete on, optimizes FTS and checkpoints the WAL; a read-only open of a pre-14 store upgrades it first.
handfixes.why: Codex r2 found the shape-based filter kept leaking: (1) an install upgraded from 0.1.16 kept `password` in SQLite because the keep-richer merge retains keys the filtered incoming row lacks, so MCP sql `SELECT data FROM asset_passwords WHERE id='7'` returned it after sync; (2) a vault 422 body {"errors":{"password":["rejected value: SECRET"]}} passed because the secret was inside an array, and `asset-passwords create` printed it. Redirects into the vault, text/HTML error bodies, the `_at` suffix pass (otp_secret_at) and password-type asset field values (no type on the asset, only on its layout) leaked the same way. The rule lives in hand files plus calls in the GENERATED client.go and store.go; a reprint regenerates those without the calls, every test still compiles (the methods stay defined), and the secrets leak again with a green build.

handfixes.summary: audit completeness, layout-drift and summary read asset values from Hudu's read shape `fields` ({label,value}) as well as `custom_fields`; audit stale-passwords checks the sync record under its real name asset-passwords
handfixes.why: Hudu returns an asset's values under `fields` as label/value objects on reads (HuduAPI module Set-HuduAsset.ps1 reshapes $_.fields label/value) and takes `custom_fields` only on writes. The audits read only custom_fields, so a fully filled asset scored 0% complete and every field was reported missing. stale-passwords looked up the sync record asset_passwords while sync records asset-passwords, so it always printed the never-synced hint. Publish review round 1 (adversarial P1, Codex/adversarial P2).

Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
